analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows: Rates Vol Taking A Toll
key_insights: Aggregate equity positioning is resilient at modestly overweight levels (0.27sd, 60th percentile) and moved largely sideways this week despite the surge in rates volatility.

Large-cap positioning is overweight but not extreme (0.58sd, 85th percentile) and well below levels implied by the earnings boom. Small-cap positioning slipped to modestly underweight (-0.13sd, 43rd percentile).

Systematic strategies hold firm at elevated levels (0.99sd, 92nd percentile, top decile) and are vulnerable to higher equity vol. Discretionary positioning fell to below neutral (-0.28sd, 27th-29th percentile).

Discretionary large-cap positioning has also fallen over recent weeks (68th percentile). The decline matches the rise in rates vol, which DB says is the key driver for equities, not the level of rates. Correlation of the 1m MOVE index with large-cap discretionary positioning is -62% since 2021.
Sector positioning is narrow. MCG & Tech (0.83sd, 82nd percentile) is the only clear overweight. Energy is around neutral (69th percentile). Other cyclicals and defensives are at or below neutral.

The rotation into Tech gained another 2pp of outperformance this week. The MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 is getting close to the top of its long-run trend channel (14.2% annualized trend since 2016, +/-10% band), from which it has reversed several times before.

Vol-control funds' equity allocation is at the 98th percentile. Sell-off sensitivity rose before easing from earlier-week levels. Capacity to add equities is limited and the flow backdrop is asymmetric, becoming less supportive if volatility rises.

CTA equity positioning declined this week but is elevated (77th percentile). The US is at the 91st percentile, Europe 79th, EM 76th and Japan 60th. Further additions depend more on falling volatility than on stronger trend signals.

CTAs remain extreme short bonds (US 11th percentile, Europe 12th percentile) and long the dollar (96th percentile). They are short gold (15th percentile) and strongly long copper (98th percentile) and oil (78th percentile).

Risk parity equity allocations declined modestly but remain elevated (73rd percentile). Commodities (93rd percentile), REITs (95th percentile) and inflation hedges (95th percentile) are elevated, while bonds are below norms (33rd percentile).

AAII sentiment (bull minus bear) turned less bearish but marked a fourth straight bearish week (16th percentile). Bearish responses are at the 92nd percentile and neutral responses at the 6th percentile.

Call-to-put volume ratio (5d ma) fell this week (82nd percentile) on lower net call volume in single stocks and indices, led by MCG & Tech. S&P 500 3m 90-110 skew rose. Total net call volume is at the 98th percentile.

Weekly fund flows: equity funds +$15.8bn after last week's outflows, led by DM equities (+$12.5bn). US funds had a second week of outflows (-$2.7bn). Global funds +$9.6bn, Europe +$1.3bn, Japan +$1.8bn, EM +$3.2bn driven by China (+$3.7bn).

Sector fund flows: Tech +$3.3bn (largest weekly inflow in a month), Utilities +$1.0bn (largest YTD), Real Estate and Telecom +$0.8bn each. Industrials -$0.5bn (second week of outflows), Energy -$0.3bn, Consumer Goods -$0.2bn.
Bond funds took in $18.8bn. Government bonds drew $10.8bn (highest in four months) and munis $4.2bn (record). IG funds moved to outflows (-$1.1bn) and HY and MBS each lost $1.4bn.
Money market funds had outflows of $118.0bn, led by the US (-$78.0bn). Europe (-$38.5bn) saw its largest outflows on record.
Large-cap mutual fund beta to the S&P 500 is low (1m rolling 23rd percentile, 3m 16th percentile), while equity L/S hedge fund beta is high (1m 78th percentile, 3m 93rd percentile).
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $358, 2027 EPS $420. S&P 500 announced buybacks over 3 months total $192bn.

tension_points.bull_case: Aggregate positioning is resilient at the 60th percentile, large caps are overweight but not extreme (85th percentile) and below levels implied by the earnings boom, and systematic strategies hold at the 92nd percentile.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising rates vol has pulled discretionary positioning below neutral (27th percentile) and small caps to underweight. Systematic positioning (92nd percentile) and vol-control funds (98th percentile) are vulnerable if equity vol rises.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher equity vol, which would trigger systematic de-risking given vol-control allocation at the 98th percentile and limited capacity to add.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech drew its largest weekly fund inflow in a month, MCG & Tech positioning is the only clear overweight, and the MCG & Tech ratio gained another 2pp this week.
tension_points.bear_case: The ratio is approaching the top of its long-run trend channel, from which it has reversed several times previously.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 reaching the top of its trend channel (14.2% annualized trend since 2016, +/-10% band), where past reversals occurred.
